questions.question: How to represent prepared producer inputs and stable identities without introducing a new canonical protocol?
questions.proposal: Select a closed bounded helper/CLI draft input mapped to existing full-revision manifest and exact files. Caller-supplied valid IDs persist unchanged; if allocation is supported for a new intent, record allocated IDs once in an exclusive recoverable draft before publication. Review input trust and replay rules first.

questions.question: Which no-overwrite atomic Windows publication primitive meets the existing contract?
questions.proposal: Choose and independently test a native same-volume primitive with no replacement flag, flushed READY.pending and explicit collision/fault outcomes. Do not use replacement rename or claim untested durability; unavailable primitive is a technical block, not permission to simulate success.

limitations: Prepared synthetic drafts only, no real Bank/install/editor/UI/release acceptance
Portable fixture cannot prove Windows ACL/NTFS/atomic publication
Trusted owner/operator/code/root parents; no malicious admin or same-owner adversary resistance
Process death and FlushFileBuffers/MoveFileExW tests do not prove physical power-loss durability
Existing incomplete package never repaired or automatically removed; explicit matching pending resume only
Publication is not Bank acceptance; external refs/CAS and durable accepted receipts belong to app
Native directory junction/hardlink exercised; no claim of a separate file-symlink privilege-dependent subtype test
Published helper validates structure and incoming exact references only; external accepted refs, stale bases and genealogy cycles remain app-owned
All mandatory scoped checks available; actual UI and production acceptance remain future tasks
